To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a winner-take all computation can be implemented in a spiking VLSI network, that this network performs feature competition, and that the feature competition is fast.

(1) the feature competition can be implemented in a network of spiking neurons; (2) this network can be implemented in VLSI; (3) the network can be trained to select the best of several competing feature maps.
a VLSI implementation of a spiking network that performs a winner-takeall computation has been developed and demonstrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a VLSI implementation of spiking neural networks for the purpose of performing feature competition.
developing a VLSI implementation of a recurrent neural network that can be trained to learn a set of input-output mappings.
the design of a VLSI system that can perform the computation of a winner-takeall network of neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has shown that it is possible to build a VLSI system of spiking neurons that can perform the feature competition task in a manner consistent with biological networks.
, in general, the winner-take-all circuit can be used for a variety of tasks in which the winner of a competitive process is required to perform some action, and the loser is required to do nothing.
the results obtained in this study show that a winner-take- all computation can be implemented in a network of integrate-and-fire spiking neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed, fabricated and tested a VLSI circuit that implements a recurrent spiking network with a feature competition capability.
we have demonstrated a winner-take all network in spiking VLSI and in a network of neurons, and that we have demonstrated feature competition between two networks.
we have demonstrated that the feature competition can be performed by a VLSI circuit that is made up of integrate-and-fire neuron circuits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the winner-take-all functionality of the chip can be used to implement a feature competition task, and that it is possible to perform this computation with a network of integrate-and-fire spiking neurons.
the winner-take-all operation can be achieved by using a recurrent network of integrate-and-fire neuron models.
recurrent VLSI networks can be configured to perform a winner-takes-all computation in a spiking framework.
